extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on personalized news recommendation, recommender systems, NLP and data-mining
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation dimensions for building and researching personalized news recommendation systems, covering core problems (news/user modeling, ranking, training), datasets, evaluation metrics, and responsible-AI concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: System workflow / key components
rubrics_metrics.description: An example workflow: Visit → Recall candidate news from a large-scale news pool → Personalized ranking of candidates according to inferred user interests → Display top-K news → Record user behaviors and update user profile for future serving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design must handle candidate recall and efficient ranking; components include recall (candidate generation), news modeling, user modeling, ranking objective, model training, evaluation, and online update. Consider where each algorithmic technique fits into this pipeline when designing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: News modeling (feature-based vs deep learning-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: News modeling aims to understand content and characteristics of news. Two main paradigms: feature-based (handcrafted features like TF-IDF variants, entities, topics, publisher, recency, popularity) and deep learning-based (neural models that learn representations from raw text such as CNNs, self-attention, and pre-trained language models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature-based methods require domain knowledge and can suffer from suboptimal semantic representation; ID-based (collaborative) representations lead to severe cold-start for fresh news. Deep models (including PLMs like BERT) can better capture semantics but may be computationally heavier. Use multimodal and knowledge-aware features where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Features for news representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Main types of features used for news: XF-IDF/BOW variants (CF-IDF, SF-IDF), entity/keyword features, cluster/category/topic distributions (LDA), emotion/sentiment, knowledge graph / ontology, visual information, property features (category, location, publisher), and context features (popularity, CTR, recency, novelty, timestamp, dwell time, bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine semantic, property, and context features as needed. Property features are usually static after publishing; context features are dynamic and capture freshness/attractiveness. Hybrid approaches mix IDs and content/features to mitigate cold-start. Examples and variants (e.g., SF-IDF, CF-IDF, SF-IDF+) are given; multimodal and knowledge-aware approaches can improve representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: User modeling (feature-based vs deep learning-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: User modeling aims to infer personal user interests from profiles/behaviors. Approaches: feature-based (user IDs, aggregated clicked-news features, demographics, location, access patterns) and deep learning-based (RNNs/GRU on click sequences, hierarchical interest representations, personalized attention networks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature-based user models require manual feature engineering and can be sparse; neural models can learn deep interest representations from clicks but must handle noisy/implicit feedback. Consider hierarchical, session-based, and personalized-attention designs to capture diverse and dynamic interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized ranking (relevance, fine-grained matching, exploration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ranking orders candidate news by relevance to user interest. Methods measure user-news relevance via representation similarity (cosine, inner product), pairwise/pointwise classifiers (SVM), or fine-grained matching (e.g., CNN-based matching between candidate and clicked news). Reinforcement learning / contextual bandits can optimize long-term reward and support exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple relevance-only ranking risks creating filter bubbles by recommending similar items to past clicks. Use exploration-aware methods (LinUCB, deep RL such as DRN, DBGD) to balance exploitation and exploration and mitigate filter bubbles. Consider fine-grained interaction/matching architectures for better relevance estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model training objectives and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Most models are trained on implicit feedback (clicks). Training techniques include binary classification with cross-entropy, negative sampling (pairing positives with negatives), and objectives beyond clicks (predicting reading satisfaction, dwell time). Click signals are noisy and may not equal satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design engagement-aware training objectives (e.g., jointly predict clicks and satisfaction) to better capture true user need. Apply negative sampling carefully; be mindful of noise in click labels. Consider multi-objective optimization that includes engagement and long-term reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: metrics, offline vs online, and unbiased evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Common evaluation metrics: classification metrics (AUC, F1), ranking metrics (MRR, nDCG), and engagement metrics (dwell time, dislike). Most work uses offline evaluation, but offline data are biased by prior recommenders; online A/B tests provide better real-world signals. There is a need for unbiased offline evaluation methods for contextual bandit-based recommenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of accuracy and engagement metrics to assess quality. Prefer online evaluations where possible; when using offline tests, account for selection bias (e.g., use unbiased evaluation methods for contextual bandits). Report both offline and online results when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets and benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Public datasets (e.g., plista, Adressa, MIND) and public leaderboards/competitions are important for reproducible research and fair comparisons. However, many studies use proprietary datasets collected from various news platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use large-scale public datasets (MIND is highlighted) and public leaderboards to benchmark models; be aware that proprietary datasets limit reproducibility. Dataset choice influences the problems you can study (e.g., Adressa includes dwell time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible news recommendation (privacy, diversity, fairness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond accuracy, responsible aspects include user privacy (privacy-preserving training and serving, e.g., federated learning), diversity to alleviate filter bubbles, and fairness to mitigate biased outcomes learned from biased data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate federated or privacy-aware frameworks for model training and serving. Use diversity-aware ranking or objectives to increase information variety. Apply fairness-aware machine learning techniques (e.g., FairRec, adversarial methods) to reduce disparate impacts; systematically evaluate responsibility dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold-start and temporal dynamics of news
rubrics_metrics.description: News items have short life cycles: many new articles emerge daily and old ones expire, causing severe cold-start challenges. User interests are dynamic. Recency and novelty are crucial context features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pure ID-based representations for news because they fail on cold-start. Use content-based or hybrid representations, incorporate recency/popularity/context features, and design models that adapt quickly to newly published items (e.g., content encoders, session-aware methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias in feedback and dataset influence from prior recommenders
rubrics_metrics.description: Offline data are influenced by predecessor recommendation algorithms, creating selection bias; click feedback can be noisy and confounded by item exposure. This hampers fair/offline evaluation and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt debiasing techniques and unbiased evaluation approaches (e.g., contextual bandit evaluation, counterfactual methods). Collect diverse feedback signals (dwell time, dislikes, reading speed) and consider methods that explicitly model exposure bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability and candidate recall efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommender systems must recall a small set of candidate news from a very large, high-velocity news pool before ranking; this demands scalable candidate generation and efficient indexing/representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design scalable recall modules (embedding-based nearest neighbors, inverted indices, filtering by metadata) that balance computational cost and candidate quality. Consider unified models that handle both recall and ranking or efficient two-stage pipelines.
